# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 50–59/100, Needs work Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 11.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 50. High = (11.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 59. All results below are read from code. The score is held down by three things: - The site renders only in the browser, so the served HTML is an empty shell. - The `/guides` page is marked noindex. - The home page reaches `/guides` only through a button click, not a link. The one unknown is which domain your canonical links should use. ## Live check **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Turn on server rendering so pages ship real content - **Why it matters:** with `ssr: false`, the HTML a crawler downloads is an empty shell. The headings and text only appear after JavaScript runs, so tools that don't run JavaScript see nothing. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small. Remove the line, or keep it and prerender `/` and `/guides` instead. - **Score after this:** 63–72 ### 2. Make the sitemap pointer in robots.txt an absolute URL - **Why it matters:** the sitemap spec requires a full URL on the `Sitemap:` line. A relative path may be ignored, so crawlers may never find your sitemap through robots.txt. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small. Use `Sitemap: https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`, or your real domain. - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 3. Link to the guides page with a real link - **Why it matters:** crawlers follow `` links, not button clicks. Right now `/guides` has no link pointing to it on any page. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Replace it with `Trail guides`. - **Score after this:** 59–67 The next biggest item is the `/guides` noindex, listed under GEO-014 below. Fixing it alone gives 57–65. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and well-formed | Clear | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, tiny, valid lines. The relative `Sitemap:` line is scored under GEO-011. | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-2`: only `/admin` is disallowed for `*`. I assumed you want to be found. | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`: `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` for `/guides`, which is listed at `public/sitemap.xml:4`. 1 of 2 routes clear. `/admin` is deliberately noindex and left out. | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical link | Can't tell | No canonical set anywhere. No domain is declared except the `trailhead.example` placeholder in the sitemap. | | GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | `nuxt.config.ts:2`: `ssr: false,`. No prerender config found. 0 of 2 routes clear. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found anywhere. | | GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4`: `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml`. The sitemap file itself is valid. | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | `app.vue:2` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` set one title and description for every page. The home page is fine and `/guides` repeats them. `lang` is set at `nuxt.config.ts:5`. 1 of 2 routes clear. | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by real links | Problem | `pages/index.vue:8`: `/guides` is reached only through a button. 0 of 1 route clear. | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet` in `headers.ts`, the pages or the config. | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Read `app.vue` and the three pages. They have no images, the button has text, and there is a title. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | No app profile declared. | | GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | Not present. This is information only. | | GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | None present. | ## Other problems found None found beyond the scored results above. ## Worth considering - **Fill in the guides page:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. The page promises graded routes but lists none. Add the routes with their grades, distance and difficulty as text. - **Give each route its own page:** the same line implies a list. Pages like `/guides/` would give each walk its own address and page title, and let you link them from `/guides`. - **Add text to the home page:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. The only content is a heading and a button. Add a short intro covering what the walks are and who they suit. - **Set a title and description per page:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' })`. Use `useHead` or `useSeoMeta` in each page. For example, `/guides` could be "Trail guides: graded Peak District walks | Trailhead". - **Add canonical links:** no canonical is set anywhere. Once you confirm the real domain, add one per page, such as `https:///guides`. - **Declare the site's URL:** `nuxt.config.ts` has no site URL. Set one, for example in `runtimeConfig.public`, so canonicals, the sitemap and social tags all share one origin. - **Add site identity data:** `app.vue:2` names the site "Trailhead", but nothing says so in machine-readable form. `WebSite` or `Organization` JSON-LD could carry the name and URL. - **Add social tags:** `nuxt.config.ts:6` has only a description. Adding `og:title`, `og:description` and `og:image` improves link previews. - **Add `` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-4` list URLs with no dates. Add real last-modified dates if you have them. - **Generate the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml` is hand-kept, so it will go stale as you add guides. A Nuxt sitemap module could build it from your routes. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015:** no canonical is set and the real domain isn't declared. Tell me the domain, then I can say what the canonical on each page should be. - **GEO-003:** a hosting layer could prerender pages outside this repo. The code suggests an empty shell, and a live check would confirm it. - **GEO-014 and GEO-017:** CDN or hosting headers outside the repository aren't visible. The `X-Robots-Tag` middleware runs only when Nitro serves the site, so a purely static host would skip it. That would also change the result for `/guides`. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI tools to find this site. - `/admin` is deliberately private, so its noindex and robots.txt disallow are not counted as problems. - I read `app.vue`, `nuxt.config.ts`, all three pages, `public/robots.txt`, `public/sitemap.xml` and `server/middleware/headers.ts`. That is the whole repository: 3 routes, no `geo.config.json`, no JSON-LD and no other `robots.txt` or sitemap source. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
